subtitle: When Copper Spoke in the Name of the Boar-Emblem King

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a royal hall, with a copper plate and boar seal glowing in the foreground
panels.action: Vikramaditya I of Badami sits upright on a carved throne as royal scribes kneel before him, a freshly inscribed copper plate lying between them, its heavy boar seal catching the lamplight in a Deccan palace hall.

dialogue.text: In the Deccan age of Vikramaditya I, the Chalukya boar seal bound king, land and village with words etched in copper.

i18n.hi: विक्रमादित्य प्रथम के दक्खन युग में चालुक्य सूअर-मोहर ने तांबे पर खुदे शब्दों से राजा, जमीन और गाँव को बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye over the Deccan plateau with inset of Badami cliff temples
panels.action: From high above the rocky Deccan plateau, the scene sweeps over scattered villages, fields and rivers before settling on the sandstone cliffs and cave shrines of Badami, where Vikramaditya I’s capital clings to the red rock.

dialogue.text: The mid-seventh century Deccan was a land of stone hills, dry fields and busy roads, where the Chalukyas of Badami ruled from their red cliffs.

i18n.hi: सातवीं सदी के बीच का दक्खन पत्थरीले पहाड़ों, सूखे खेतों और व्यस्त सड़कों की भूमि था, जहाँ बादामी के चालुक्य लाल चट्टानों से राज करते थे।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of the royal audience hall
panels.action: In a pillared hall, Vikramaditya I sits in council, calm yet alert, while Brahmin advisers and officers stand around, scrolls and palm-leaf bundles in hand, a map of villages laid on a low table before them.

dialogue.text: Vikramaditya I, son of Pulakeshin’s line, fought rivals and rebuilt power, but ruling meant more than war; it meant reaching every village with order that could endure.

i18n.hi: पुलकेशिन की वंश-रेखा के पुत्र विक्रमादित्य प्रथम ने दुश्मनों से लड़ा, शक्ति फिर जुटाई, पर राज सिर्फ युद्ध नहीं था; हर गाँव तक टिकाऊ अनुशासन पहुँचाना भी था।

panels.shot: close-up on a royal scribe’s hands holding old copper plates
panels.action: A royal scribe kneels at the king’s feet, carefully lifting a stack of darkened copper plates tied with a cord, each showing faint engravings and an embossed boar emblem worn smooth by use.

dialogue.text: Already for generations, kings across India had used copper plates to record grants; now the Chalukyas made them the firm spine of their Deccan rule.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियों से भारत भर के राजा ताम्रपत्रों पर दान लिख रहे थे; अब चालुक्यों ने इन्हें अपने दक्खन राज का कड़ा कंधा बना दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Brahmin petitioner before the throne
panels.action: A dignified Brahmin from a distant village bows deeply before Vikramaditya I, holding a palm-leaf petition, while behind him a small group of followers wait nervously, dusty from travel.

dialogue.text: From far villages like Kollapur and Peddavaduguru, Brahmin settlers and temple men came to Badami, seeking royal land grants in return for ritual, learning and support.

i18n.hi: कोल्लापुर, पेड्डावडुगूर जैसे दूर गाँवों से ब्राह्मण बसाहटें और मंदिर के लोग बादामी पहुँचते, कि वेद, पूजा और सहारे के बदले राजदानी जमीन-दान पा सकें।

panels.shot: close-up profile of Vikramaditya I in thought
panels.action: Vikramaditya I leans slightly forward on his throne, eyes steady, fingers resting on the armrest as he listens, a faint frown of calculation on his face while the court stands silent.

dialogue.speaker: vikramaditya_i_and_chalukya_scribes
dialogue.text: If I grant, it must bind my officers yet outlast my reign.

i18n.hi: जो भी दूँ, वह मेरे अफ़सरों को बाँधे, और मेरे राज के बाद भी चले।

panels.shot: medium shot of scribes seated on the floor writing
panels.action: Royal scribes sit cross-legged on a mat, one reading from a palm leaf, another carefully tracing letters on bright copper plates laid before him, while a junior assistant grinds metal styluses beside them.

dialogue.text: In the writing office, scribes turned petitions into royal charters, following a precise order of praises, boundaries, taxes and commands for future officials.

i18n.hi: लेखन-कार्यालय में लेखकों ने अरज़ियों को राजाधिकार-पत्रों में बदला, स्तुति, सीमा, कर और भावी अफ़सरों के हुक्म की तय पटकथा पर।

panels.shot: close-up on the engraved text on the copper plate
panels.action: The camera lingers on the copper plate as a stylus carves neat Nagari and Kannada-tinged letters, marking out lines that mention Vikramaditya’s titles, the land of Kollapur, and clauses of tax and protection.

dialogue.text: The Kollapur plates of Vikramaditya I set down in metal which fields, which streams, which trees marked the gift, and what dues were lifted or owed.

i18n.hi: विक्रमादित्य प्रथम के कोल्लापुर ताम्रपत्रों ने धातु पर जड़ दिया कि कौन से खेत, कौन सी धार, कौन से पेड़ दान हैं, और कौन से लगान हटे या रहने हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of the scribe dictating to assistants in the hall
panels.action: A senior scribe stands before junior clerks, reciting portions of the charter as they repeat softly, correcting a line about immunities, while in the background a tax officer watches, arms folded.

dialogue.text: These grants did not equalize the village; they set apart Brahmins, temples and officers with special rights, lifting some taxes while confirming others.

i18n.hi: इन दानों ने गाँव को बराबर नहीं किया; इन्होंने ब्राह्मणों, मंदिरों और अमलों को ख़ास हक़ देकर अलग किया, कुछ कर घटाए, कुछ को पक्का किया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Vikramaditya I reviewing the finished plate
panels.action: A scribe respectfully presents the gleaming Kollapur copper plate to Vikramaditya I, who inspects the engraved lines and nods once, the court watching as though the metal now carries his voice.

dialogue.text: When the king approved, the words became more than ink; they became a royal order carried in copper, addressed even to officers yet unborn.

i18n.hi: राजा की मुहर पड़ते ही शब्द स्याही से आगे बढ़ गए; वे तांबे पर ढली राज-आज्ञा बने, उन अफ़सरों तक को संबोधित जो अभी जन्मे भी न थे।

panels.shot: close-up on the boar seal being pressed onto the plate’s ring
panels.action: A craftsman’s strong hands guide a small metal seal bearing the Chalukya boar emblem onto the ring that binds the plates, pressing it firmly so that the animal form stands proud and unmistakable.

dialogue.text: At the clasp, the boar of the Chalukyas was stamped in relief, a sign that this was not mere contract, but a piece of the king’s own authority.

i18n.hi: क्लैस्प पर चालुक्यों का सूअर उभरा हुआ ठप्पा था, निशान कि यह साधा सौदा नहीं, राजा की खुद की हुकूमत का टुकड़ा है।

panels.shot: medium shot of the formal grant ceremony in court
panels.action: In the royal hall, Vikramaditya I hands the sealed copper charter to the lead Brahmin donee, who receives it with both hands and bowed head, while courtiers and officers stand as witnesses in ordered rows.

dialogue.text: Witnesses were named, curses on violators recited, and the plate was entrusted to the donee, to be read aloud whenever officials questioned its claims.

i18n.hi: गवाहों के नाम लिखे गए, तोड़ने वालों पर श्राप पढ़े गए, और तख्ती दान पाने वाले के हवाले हुई, ताकि अमलदार शक करें तो ज़ोर से पढ़ कर सुनाई जाए।

panels.shot: wide shot of the village outskirts with markers and farmers
panels.action: On the outskirts of a Deccan village, the Brahmin donee stands with local elders, pointing to rocks, trees and an irrigation channel, while farmers watch as officials mark these as the grant’s boundaries.

dialogue.text: Out in the fields, stone, tree and canal were tied to the king’s words, so no officer could later pretend the lines were unclear.

i18n.hi: खेतों में पत्थर, पेड़ और नाला राजा के शब्दों से बाँधे गए, ताकि कोई अफ़सर बाद में न कह सके कि सीमाएँ धुंधली थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a village household reacting to the grant
panels.action: Inside a thatched house, a farming family listens as a village headman explains that some lands now fall under Brahmin and temple control, their faces a mix of acceptance, concern and curiosity about what this will change.

dialogue.text: For common villagers, the plate did not grant equal voice; it often shifted dues from one hand to another, tightening ties between village elites and the distant court.

i18n.hi: साधारण गाँववालों के लिए तख्ती ने समान आवाज़ नहीं दी; उसने अक्सर लगान बस एक हाथ से दूसरे में सरकाए, गाँव के बड़े लोगों और दूर दरबार की डोर और कसी।

panels.shot: close-up of a tax officer reading the plate years later
panels.action: Years later, a Chalukya tax officer kneels in a dusty village assembly, squinting as he traces the engraved letters on the now-tarnished copper plate while elders sit around, listening to the charter’s old commands.

dialogue.text: When officials demanded dues, the plate was brought out, its clauses on exemptions and obligations read aloud, reminding the king’s servants that they too were bound.

i18n.hi: जब अमलदार लगान माँगते, तख्ती निकाली जाती, उस पर छूट और फ़र्ज़ वाले अनुच्छेद पढ़े जाते, ताकि राजा के नौकर भी याद रखें कि वे भी बँधे हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a road with traders and a temple settlement
panels.action: A busy Deccan road runs past newly built Brahmin houses and a small temple near the granted fields, as traders’ caravans move by and a toll collector sits under a tree, recording passing loads on palm leaves.

dialogue.text: Land grants drew Brahmin settlements and temples to village edges, anchoring routes of trade, tolls and learning in a network that linked local power to royal copper.

i18n.hi: जमीनी दानों ने ब्राह्मण बस्तियाँ और मंदिर गाँव की सरहदों पर बसाए, जहाँ से व्यापार, महसूल और शिक्षा के रस्ते एक जाल बन कर राज के तांबे से जुड़ गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of a later scholar examining an old plate in a modern setting
panels.action: In a modern archive room, a historian carefully examines the Kollapur copper plates under soft light, gloves on, while a magnifying glass reveals the ancient letters and the Chalukya boar seal in sharp detail.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, scholars reading these plates, like those from Kollapur, see not just piety, but the making of an early medieval state through written, durable command.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, जब विद्वान ये ताम्रपत्र पढ़ते हैं, जैसे कोल्लापुर के, उन्हें केवल भक्ति नहीं दिखती, बल्कि टिकाऊ लिखित हुक्म से बनता आरंभिक मध्यकालीन राज्य दिखता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of archaeologists at Madapura Lake site
panels.action: By the calm waters of Madapura Lake near Davangere, field archaeologists gently lift a newly found inscribed stone from the soil, while a note labels it as bearing Vikramaditya I’s name under a temporary shelter.

dialogue.text: Recent finds near Madapura Lake, bearing Vikramaditya I’s name, show how new inscriptions still refine our map of his reach and of Chalukya administration.

i18n.hi: मदापुर झील के पास मिली नई ताम्र-खोजें, जिन पर विक्रमादित्य प्रथम का नाम है, दिखाती हैं कि कैसे नए लेख अभी भी उसके प्रभाव और चालुक्य शासन का नक्शा निखार रहे हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the boar seal in close-up, tarnished yet clear
panels.action: The scene closes on a close-up of the tarnished boar seal on the Kollapur plate, its lines softened by age yet still firm, resting on a table between a historian’s notes and a faint outline of the Deccan map.

dialogue.text: So the boar seal of Vikramaditya I reminds us that just rule rests not only on courage in battle, but on records that villages, elites and officials alike can trust across generations.

i18n.hi: तो विक्रमादित्य प्रथम की सूअर-मोहर याद दिलाती है कि न्यायी राज सिर्फ रण-साहस पर नहीं, उन दस्तावेज़ों पर भी टिकता है जिन पर गाँव, बड़े और अफ़सर पीढ़ियों तक भरोसा कर सकें।

title_i18n.en: The Boar Seal Grants a Village

subtitle_i18n.en: When Copper Spoke in the Name of the Boar-Emblem King
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब तांबा बोला सूअर-चिह्न वाले राजा के नाम पर
